title: Staged simulations for batching & KV-cache suggestions and revertable apply flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams running high-volume inference are frequently presented with automated batching and KV-cache recommendations, but they lack a low-friction way to understand the runtime impact and recover safely from config changes. Current recommendation cards show estimated savings but do not let customers validate changes against a live-like simulation or stage config changes in a revertable sandbox.

Goal: Build a console-first staged-simulation flow for Optimize recommendation cards that lets users: 1) preview the runtime and cost impact via an inline simulation (sample traces and token-level breakdowns), 2) stage config changes to a tenant-scoped sandbox environment, and 3) apply changes with an easily accessible rollback path and audit trail. The flow should minimize cognitive overhead while preserving observability and compliance needs.

What success looks like: increased adoption of batching/caching recommendations (target +25% accepted suggestions in 60 days), reduced support tickets about regressions after recommendation applies (target -40%), and clear auditability for enterprise customers.

Constraints & assumptions: staged sandbox will run against replayed traffic samples (not production live traffic) and must tie back to the recommendation card and the originating evaluation dataset. We will re-use existing telemetry and cost-estimation services from Optimize. Rollback must be a single-click action that triggers an explicit revert plan in the runtime control plane.

Non-goals: this ticket does not include adding new recommendation heuristics or making changes to the serving runtime itself—those are separate ENG initiatives.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards include a 'Simulate impact' CTA that opens an inline panel with sample trace visualization and token-level cost delta for the top 3 affected routes.
Users can stage a recommendation to a tenant-scoped sandbox environment for a configurable duration; staging creates a record in the Apply History with a unique staging ID.
Staged changes expose a single-click 'Revert staging' that marks the staging as rejected and records a rollback audit entry with timestamp and actor.

Applying a staged config produces an 'Apply run' entry in the Apply History that links to runtime rollout progress and an automated smoke-check summary (latency, error rate, quality regressions on a small eval set).
Apply History entries include who initiated the action, a diff preview, simulation summary, and links to the originating recommendation card and related PR/Dashboard.
Perf & cost telemetry for simulations aligns within +/- 20% of a controlled test replay of production traces for the same window (measured in QA).
Design sign-off from Console UX and Security checklist completed for tenant-scoped sandboxes.
